newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Wendy's net rose 26 percent in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Wendy's net rose 26 percent in quarter.

text.p: Wendy's International Inc. said Tuesday its earnings rose 26 percent in the first quarter, as higher sales more than offset increased costs for beef for its hamburgers.

The Dublin, Ohio-based restaurant chain said profits rose to $24.6 million, or 19 cents a share, in the quarter, from $19.5 million, or 16 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales rose 12 percent to $459 million from $410 million.
Systemwide sales, including franchises and the Tim Hortons chain of restaurants, rose 12 percent to $1.36 billion from $1.21 billion.
Results were aided by comparisons to a 1996 quarter when stormy winter weather hurt sales, Wendy's Chairman Gordon Teter said in a statement.

The results were a penny shy of average forecasts on Wall Street of 20 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates, but Wendy's stock rose 37.5 cents to $21.125 amid a broad rally on the New York Stock Exchange.

Sales at company-owned restaurants rose more than 9 percent per unit in the quarter and that helped offset higher costs for beef and tomatoes and costs for training more employees to make and serve pita sandwiches, Wendy's said.

Earnings were hurt by one-time charges related to international operations and store closings, the company said, as well as the Easter holiday, which fell in the first quarter in 1997 but in the second quarter last year.
Wendy's said it started converting 28 former Hardee's in the Detroit area and 25 former Rax restaurants in Columbus, Ohio, and West Virginia to Tim Hortons outlets.
Wendy's also said it agreed to buy three Back Yard Burger restaurants in Columbus, which will be converted to Tim Hortons.
